READABILITY.evidence: Names are mostly clear (openDangerConfirm, updateAfterSalePreview, currentAfterSaleOrderId). But the 3.5k-line file has very few comments, and the long inline delegation handlers rely on short names like `e`, `a` and `cb`.

MAINTAINABILITY.evidence: One 3573-line file. initEvents() wires every listener inline (pay/ship/cancel/aftersale/backup/reset/danger modal) and clearly runs well over 100 lines, which triggers the >100-line cap. UI handlers call shopTestAPI.* directly as their business layer.

ROBUSTNESS.evidence: Inputs are validated (after-sale qty `Number.isInteger(val) || val < 0`, import errors). There is a silent `try { navigator.clipboard.writeText(...) } catch (_) {}`, though not on a mutation path. Hidden tests failed on seed products and out-of-stock rejection, so some edge cases are not covered.

C9-01-CASE1.evidence: openDangerConfirm is used for cancel (with the refund amount shown), restock and reset, and errors surface as toasts. Import overwrite runs `shopTestAPI.importData` without any confirmation, and after-sale submit has no explicit confirm beyond the modal preview.

C9-01-CASE2.evidence: The UI routes all operations through shopTestAPI (pay/ship/cancel/requestAfterSale/importData), so the logic is shared. Money uses float math with `round2(order.payable - order.refundedAmount)` and `.toFixed(2)` rather than integer cents.
